newsitem.title: ESTONIA: Maersk Air completes privatization of Estonia Air.
newsitem.headline: Maersk Air completes privatization of Estonia Air.

text.p: The privatization of Estonia's national flag carrier by Denmark's Maersk Air has been completed, company officials said on Wednesday.
"The privatization of Estonia Air has just been successfully completed and we are proud to be one of the new owners," Bjarne Hansen, president of Maersk Air, told a news conference.
"In the next three years, we will invest 40 million kroons," Hansen said.
Maersk Air is controlled by the Danish group AP Moeller.
In June, the Estonian privatization agency decided to sell 66 percent of the state-run airline to a joint bid by Denmark's Maersk Air and its Estonian partner Baltic Cresco Investment.
The agency said Maersk and Cresco paid 60 million kroons for their stake.
He added that as of October 27, Estonian Air would use only western aircraft. The company's four Russian-built Yakovlevs would shortly be replaced by two Fokker-50s, Hansen said.
The company currently has two Boeing 737-500s.
Estonia Air concluded a code share agreement with Finnair on Wednesday and plans a similiar agreement with Dutch airline KLM.
"Finnair and KLM have displayed a very positive attitude toward Estonia Air," Hansen said. "But SAS apparently does not want to have Estonia Air around."
After bidding unsuccessfully for Estonia Air, SAS (Scandinavian Airlines System) terminated a ground service agreement at Tallinn Airport with Estonia Air.
Hansen said the new management of Estonia Air wanted to restore flights between Tallinn and Copenhagen, which Estonia Air was forced to drop because of stiff competition from SAS.
SAS is partially owned by the governments of Sweden, Denmark and Norway.
